blocks.h2: Signs Your Sump Pump Needs Attention
blocks.intro: Don't wait for the next storm:

tiles.body: A stuck float, a failed check valve or an undersized pump.
A jammed impeller or a failing motor.
If the power fails, the pump stops.

blocks.intro: In April 2013, Hinsdale declared a state of emergency as heavy rain flooded low-lying roads and Salt Creek rose. Storms like that are when a sump pump has to work.

items.body: A failed pump can damage flooring, walls and furniture in a few hours.
Storms and power outages often arrive together. A backup keeps the pit from overflowing.
Some older basements have small or shallow pits. We can enlarge or replace them.
We route the discharge away from the foundation and protect it from freezing.

blocks.h2: Sump Pump Questions From Hinsdale Homeowners

items.q: Do we need a battery backup sump pump?
items.preview: If the basement is finished, yes.
items.answer: If your basement is finished or holds anything valuable, yes. Heavy storms often knock out power.

items.q: How long do sump pumps last?
items.answer: Most last about 7 to 10 years, less if they run often.

items.q: Can you install a sump pump in a basement that doesn't have one?
items.answer: Often. We can install a new pit and pump where water collects, along with a discharge line to the outside.

items.q: Where should the sump pump discharge?
items.preview: Away from the house, never into the sewer.
items.answer: Away from the foundation, onto the yard or into a storm line. Never into the sanitary sewer.

items.q: Should we have a second pump for a large basement?
items.answer: Often. A second pump in the same pit or a second pit gives you protection if one fails.

items.q: Do I need a bigger sump pump?
items.preview: If it can't keep up in storms, maybe.
items.answer: If it runs constantly in heavy rain and can't keep up, a higher-capacity pump may help.

items.q: How much does sump pump installation cost in Hinsdale?
items.preview: It depends on the pump, pit and backup. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the pump, whether a new pit is needed and whether you add a backup. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
